name: DPP4 / CD26
location: Cell surfaces and soluble blood enzyme
action: Removes two residues from an accessible N terminus, often with Pro or Ala second.
relevance: Established degradation route for GLP-1 and other selected hormones. For this vaccine, inspect whether repeated trimming reaches the epitope; assay loss does not rank its circulation rate against other enzymes.

name: ACE
location: Vascular/tissue cell surfaces; soluble blood form
relevance: Can dominate degradation of particular short peptides, such as dilute bradykinin. A terminal cut may spare a central epitope. The current partial rule gives a candidate bond, not a rate.

name: CPN
action: Removes a terminal Lys or Arg.
relevance: Direct blood-peptide trimming route when the exposed C terminus is basic. Its contribution versus ACE depends on substrate concentration and sequence.

name: CPB2 / TAFI
action: The active enzyme removes terminal Lys or Arg.
relevance: Conditional contributor: precursor abundance is not active-enzyme activity. No site is asserted here because activation was not supplied; this is a coverage gap, not a predicted event.

name: Aminopeptidase P2
action: Removes the first residue when the next residue is Pro.
relevance: Relevant to accessible N-terminal trimming, particularly alternative kinin degradation. It removes one residue, unlike DPP4; membrane access is not represented by a serum motif score.

name: FAP
location: Activated stromal cell surfaces; soluble blood form
action: N-terminal X-Pro trimming and a separate internal Gly-Pro cleavage route.
relevance: The internal route can split an epitope; the terminal route can trim a flank. Tissue context and soluble activity matter. Published substrate specificity does not establish a universal strength versus DPP4.

name: MME / neprilysin
action: Internal cleavage with selected hydrophobic preferences.
relevance: Important metabolism of selected short peptides at exposed surfaces. This broad preference rule can flag many bonds; it is weak evidence of rate and has a conservative 2-30-residue modeling scope.

name: ANPEP / CD13
location: Cell-surface enzyme; soluble forms also reported
action: N-terminal amino-acid trimming; our rule flags Ala only.
relevance: Potential trimming after surface exposure. The limited Ala flag misses other substrates; absence of a flag cannot establish resistance.

name: ENPEP / aminopeptidase A
action: Prefers removal of an acidic N-terminal residue.
relevance: Conditional surface trimming; calcium, access and the newly exposed terminus matter. A sequence flag does not imply a major bulk-serum contribution.

name: PREP / prolyl oligopeptidase
location: Mainly cytoplasmic; activity also measured in human plasma
action: Post-Pro cleavage in accessible short peptides.
relevance: A possible additional internal cut mechanism. Plasma activity is documented, but its contribution to these vaccine peptides is unmeasured; our conservative rule covers 4-30 residues.

name: Proteasome / MHC-I processing
action: Proteasomal cleavage and MHC-I processing proxies.
relevance: Pepsickle human is primary for human input; all-mammal is a sensitivity comparison. NetChop 20S learns purified-proteasome digestion; Cterm and NetCleave-I learn ligand processing. These do not set the circulation clock.

name: Cathepsins B / H / S; class-II proxy
action: Cleavage/trimming after uptake; context and pH matter.
relevance: ITCell has separate 15-, 60- and 240-minute assay matrices for each enzyme. NetCleave-II is a class-II processing proxy without enzyme identification. Neither supplies circulating peptide half-life.

name: ERAP1 / ERAP2
action: N-terminal precursor trimming for MHC-I presentation.
relevance: ERAMER scores ERAP1's first trimming step on supported short inputs; ERAP2 has a partial basic-terminus rule. Trimming can expose or overtrim an epitope. Long parent input gaps are shown separately.

name: APP1, TPP2, NPEPPS, DPP8 / DPP9
relevance: Qualitative specificity rules provide conditional processing annotations. Their scores are not blood-enzyme activity or target-loss rates.

name: THOP1 / neurolysin; LNPEP / IRAP
relevance: Current entries are observed-substrate references, not general sequence predictors. A missing reference match cannot establish protection; full original processing evidence remains available.

name: ELANE / cathepsin G
location: Neutrophil granules; can be released extracellularly
relevance: PhageScout PWM scores describe site preference, while peptide scores describe substrate enrichment. Only PWM outputs can be attached to a candidate bond. Neither defines a normal-circulation enzyme rate.

name: MMPs
location: Extracellular/tissue proteases, with activation and inhibitor control
relevance: Frozen ten-mer substrate Z-scores are supporting evidence. They do not localize an exact cut or measure epitope destruction, so no cut line or circulation rate is assigned to them.
